# Mods

What you can put on an Elektron device today: mods, custom OS builds, and the loaders and patchers that build them from **your own** stock OS file. Nothing here is hosted by Aggregat; every link goes to the author.

> **Before you flash anything:** read [hardware/common/recovery.md](../hardware/common/recovery.md) and make sure you can get back to the stock OS. Mods are unofficial, Elektron does not support them, and the authors' own words about stability are summarised below, not checked by us.

## How to read this list

- **Install via** - the loader or platform that builds the mod into your OS file (see the next table), or the project's own patcher.
- **Tested** - what the author or a cited report says: *yes, on a unit* (ran on a real device), *partly* (some builds or parts), *emulator only*, or *not stated* (the sources we read say nothing). It is a claim, not our own test.
- **Updated** - the later of the last release or post we saw and the repo's last push.
- Each device section lists mods that ran on a unit first, then the rest; unreachable projects come last. Full notes per project: [INDEX.md](README.md) and the device pages.

Data last verified 2026-11-27; generated from `data/projects.yml`.


The other lists: [DEV-TOOLS.md](DEV-TOOLS.md) (development tools), [MUSICIAN-TOOLS.md](MUSICIAN-TOOLS.md) (tools for musicians). Hardware knowledge for writing mods: [hardware/](../hardware/README.md).

## What is inside the collections

Some entries bundle many mods or modules. These are the names their repos list; each collection still appears once in its device sections.

|---|---|---|
| **Cycles Engines mods** | Model:Cycles | LiXR: Drum voice with a decimator [not stated]; SAM: Speech engine with 36 words [not stated] |
| **digi1_mods** | Digitakt (MKI) | digi101 (SH-101-style mono), digieq, digimacro, digimatrix, digimono, digipoly, digiutils, tonefx 3.2 (shop files, 2026-11-08) |
| **digikit mods** | Digitakt II, Digitone II, Syntakt | PLUCK: Plucked-string synth machine (decay, pick position, brightness, colour), loaded at run time [yes, on a unit]; Frequency shifter: Shifts every frequency by the same number of Hz, as a send effect or master insert; SPREAD splits the shift between left and right (up to 8 Hz), DRIFT and RATE move it slowly with a triangle, FDBK feeds the shifted signal back after 55 ms [emulator only]; bootscreen: Loadable boot screens (.dkbs files) in place of the stock intro [yes, on a unit]; Overdrive curves: OVR ROUTING becomes OVR TYPE: pre or post times eight curves (stock, TNH4, HARD, SOFT, TUBE, FOLD, FUZZ, SQR), and the top of the OVERDRIVE range drives harder [emulator only]; Fast USB: Sends samples to the unit over an added USB bulk interface instead of SysEx: an 8 MB file at 3.9 MB/s on a Digitone II against 0.68 MB/s over SysEx; falls back to SysEx when the link fails [yes, on a unit]; TB303: Run-time machine porting the Open303 bass-line synth (MIT) [emulator only]; LFO shapes 1: Seven extra LFO waves (STP4, PULS, HSIN, ABSN, SOFT, DUCK, WOBL), named and drawn on the MOD page [emulator only]; Track manager: Names the tracks in a SETTINGS screen and shows the active track's name while TRK + YES is held [emulator only] |
